title: Prove a binomial law for polynomial right-vector cost (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic counting proof. For the two-role right-vector alphabet over F_q[t], with base-field right vectors and arbitrary free GL2(F_q) maps, a uniformly chosen invertible target of exact entry degree D>=1 satisfies

```text
cost(M)-1 ~ Binomial(D-1, (q-1)/q).

# targets of degree D and cost r
= |GL2(F_q)| (q+1) (q-1)^r q^(D-1) binom(D-1,r-1),  1<=r<=D.
```

The mean is 1+(D-1)(q-1)/q and the variance is (D-1)(q-1)/q^2. The written proof extends the binary constant-free reduction of #4763 to arbitrary fields, then counts its unique expressions. This gives the exact all-field, all-degree distribution rather than another finite binary census. No new kappa, native supplier or selected-frontier change is claimed.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Nick Petalas #4763/#4276/#4243 supplies the binary cost question and free-map lineage. Hirosi Nagao's 1959 polynomial-matrix presentation and degree method retain their classical credit; no new group-presentation theorem is claimed. ToikY #4334, Nick Petalas #4601/#4749 and Wentao Li #4099 following #2513 retain the local/semilocal and alphabet credit. Primary sources and exact pins are in the package.

## Evidence

- Before: #4763 gives the binary cost theorem and degree-at-most-four finite histogram. After: PROOF.md gives the joint cost count and binomial law for every finite field and every exact degree.
- An independent determinant-unit enumeration matches all 63,504 literal polynomial-matrix targets: 1,536 over F2 through degree four; 3,888 over F3 through degree two; 46,080 over F4 through degree two; 12,000 over F5 through degree one. The enumeration performs 135,570 product-tail comparisons. It is not presented as a census of every rejected matrix.
- All 924 invertible degree-one paid parameter tuples pass constant splitting. All free conjugations retain the required scalar. Exact probability normalization, mean and variance pass for 480 integer pairs; non-prime-power q in those arithmetic checks does not denote a finite field. Eight control groups cover the stated boundary and mutation cases.
- Both registered warning-strict ordinary and optimized commands passed locally, timed separately at 0.61 s and 0.59 s. Package metadata and replay passed. In-memory compilation passed; optional external Python analyzers were unavailable. The largest function has 29 physical lines. Finite bounds and the managed-allocation deviation are documented in README.md.
- Committed-byte/source-history preflight passed for seven files at `4d0a6363fe4f45dd9a769f5b74d02fc5d9061ae3`. Official committed export and integrity checks passed. An optimized Git-free export replay with PATH=/nonexistent matches the complete generated final receipt. Receipts are generated on stdout and bind all six package files; the predecessor proof hash is checked against SOURCES.json.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19131579).

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal claim is a written scoped proof with bounded finite corroboration. Two roles, one polynomial variable, base-field right vectors and free base-field maps are essential to this classification. Singular endpoints, multivariate rings and restored auxiliary roles remain unclassified. Uniform exact-degree targets are the sampling measure; uniform words and degree-bounded targets have different distributions.

Native preparation, conversion, routing, control, precision, restoration, stock and a complete physical consumer remain unpriced. No complete multiplication theorem, supplier admission, independent human acceptance or formal proof-kernel review is supplied. Lean, Docker and the selected operator replay were outside scope and were not run. Every registered local command ran successfully.

## Open next questions

- Derive closed-form moments under a uniform degree-bounded target measure. The proved joint counts give a finite weighted mixture; first fix that measure and sum the mean.
- Identify one literal native polynomial-coefficient producer and price left-coefficient preparation, conversion and the complete consumer before using these counts for a supplier.

## Related open work

- #4776, head `0764ab259a8ce496a4c5d4debeed4c4e4d9f7ca4`, classifies singular square-zero radical pencils in the same formal alphabet. Its coefficient algebra and endpoints differ from our invertible F_q[t] targets. No target count or cost domain overlaps.
- #4780, head `a4436fab4164eccc498d4d9885eec68211c869de`, studies singular rank-one tuples over finite field products and the sharp component threshold. The finite product algebra differs from F_q[t]; no target census number overlaps.
- #4781, head `b838121c65e1bfd17a65466c95940eb00f12a225`, counts lifts of rank-one residues over finite local algebras and proper residue-field extensions. Those endpoints and algebras differ from the present invertible polynomial targets; no target count overlaps.

- #4787, head `4b58e8cd5690bd35cf01b0018eefa2c39a298920`, proves exact arbitrary-role costs over local algebras. F_q[t] is nonlocal. On the common constant-field two-role endpoints both formulas assign cost zero; our enumerated F2/F3 constant totals are 6 and 48, and their basis images give delta zero. The positive-degree polynomial distribution and its target totals are outside that local theorem.
- #4789, head `7fdbf8040ea9a957af0576067df2d9cb6fcf0e51`, classifies singular ordinary rank-two targets over matrix algebras. Our invertible scalar-polynomial endpoints have different coefficients and ranks, so no target count or exact-cost census overlaps.

Before DONE, this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM were listed again. All newly relevant titles and bodies were read. The two additional right-vector results are recorded above; the other additions study Schur dimensions or full-guard probabilities. No conflicting shared numerical claim was found.

Merged #4763 is the direct predecessor. At binary exact degree four its joint cost vector agrees numerically with the present `[144,432,432,144]`; summing degrees zero through four reproduces `[6,270,612,504,144]`. The six constant binary free maps also agree. The new result is the quantified all-q distribution. No other open PR studying this polynomial degree-cost quantity was found in the refreshed snapshots. The account's open PRs created since the advance claim were listed again during publication preparation.
